key_insight: EDEN is a large, anonymized Italian emergency-department notes corpus with a smaller expert-annotated subset for structured clinical information extraction.
clinical_relevance: It can help develop and evaluate language models for real-world emergency care tasks in Italian, especially extracting structured data from free-text notes.
method: Collected ~4 million fully anonymized emergency department clinical notes from Italian hospitals.
Manually annotated ~6,000 notes with a 132-item structured Case Report Form for dyspnea and loss of consciousness.
Defined mixed-label fields including numerical, categorical, binary, and mixed value types for CRF filling.
evidence_signal: The paper reports corpus statistics, annotation details, and zero-shot baseline results from Gemma-27B and MedGemma-27B for the proposed CRF-filling benchmark.
watch_item: The annotated subset is relatively small and highly imbalanced, so performance may vary across item types and rare labels.
paper_title: EDEN: A Large-Scale Corpus of Clinical Notes for Italian
